accepted.s: Which deity was worshipped in the Sarvadeva shrine, also known as Kumaraswami Sarvadevadivasa, at Nagarjunakonda?
accepted.x: The Sarvadeva shrine, also called Kumaraswami Sarvadevadivasa, was dedicated to Kartikeya.
accepted.tq: Direct deity–shrine recall.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: Who built the Sarvadeva shrine at Nagarjunakonda?
accepted.x: The Sarvadeva shrine was built by Elisri, who served as the commander of Ehuvala.
accepted.tq: Who-built-what trap using closely related rulers and commanders.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: The inscription associated with the Sarvadeva shrine at Nagarjunakonda is written in:
accepted.x: The inscription of the Sarvadeva shrine is in Sanskrit.
accepted.tq: Direct language identification.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pushpabhadraswami shrine at Nagarjunakonda:
1. It was dedicated to Shiva.
2. It followed a Gajaprishtha or elephant-back plan.
3. It was begun by Virapurushadatta and completed by Ehuvala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Pushpabhadraswami shrine was a Shaiva shrine with an elephant-back plan, begun by Virapurushadatta and completed by Ehuvala.
accepted.tq: Statement checking with builder succession and architectural-plan details.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami — Shiva — built by Elisri
accepted.x: Sarvadeva was dedicated to Kartikeya and was built by Elisri. The other pairs wrongly interchange deities or builders.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure deity–builder pair and eliminate swapped combinations.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami shrine at Nagarjunakonda was built by:
o: Shivasena, commander of Abhira king Vasusena
accepted.x: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami shrine was built by Shivasena, the commander of the Abhira king Vasusena.
accepted.tq: Builder and patron identification with a swapped-authority trap.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami shrine is correct?
o: It was dedicated to Kartikeya and its inscription was in Sanskrit.
It was dedicated to Vishnu and is regarded as the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra.
It was a Saptamatrika shrine dedicated to Hariti.
It was dedicated to Shiva and had a Gajaprishtha plan.
accepted.x: Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami was a Vishnu temple and is regarded as the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra.
accepted.tq: First-in-region question using precise temple identification.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: Hariti at Nagarjunakonda was associated with which of the following?
o: A Saptamatrika shrine and the mother goddess of children
A shrine dedicated to Kubera alone
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra
accepted.x: Hariti was regarded as the mother goddess of children and was associated with a Saptamatrika shrine.
accepted.tq: Confusable shrine-function discrimination.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consists of minor shrines at Nagarjunakonda?
o: Sri Parvataswamy, Sarvadeva, Nandikeshwara and Shiva
Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami, Kartikeya, Hariti and Navagraha
accepted.x: Nodageshwara, Nandikeshwara, Navagraha and Kubera are listed as minor shrines at Nagarjunakonda.
accepted.tq: List-based group recognition.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Brahmanical temples at Nagarjunakonda:
1. Nine Shaiva temples and one Vaishnava temple stood there.
2. The Ikshvakus built the first structural Hindu temples in India.
3. The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami was counted among the Shaiva temples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami was the Vaishnava temple among the ten temples.
accepted.tq: Split the numerical composition from the wrongly classified temple.
accepted.sec: Brahmanical shrines at Nagarjunakonda → deity (Sarvadeva, Pushpabhadraswami, Kartikeya)

accepted.s: Sriparvata is identified with which place and is also known by which traditional name?
accepted.x: Sriparvata is identified with Nagarjunakonda, or Vijayapuri, and is traditionally called Dakshina Gaya.
accepted.tq: Place–alternative name–title linkage.

accepted.s: Sriparvata was named after which philosopher?

accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang found the Sriparvata vihara neglected during his seventh-century visit.
accepted.tq: Traveller’s observation and condition recall.
accepted.sec: Acharya Nagarjuna and Sriparvata - tradition, monastery, Sri Parvataswamy identified as Buddha (Kielhorn)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two similarly named religious traditions?
o: Sriparvata was the family deity of the Vishnukundins, while Sriparvataswami was sacred to Mahayana Buddhism.
Sriparvata refers to Srisaila Mallikarjuna, whereas Sriparvataswami refers to Vijayapuri.
Sriparvataswami was the family deity of the Vishnukundins and is identified with Srisaila Mallikarjuna, whereas Sriparvata refers to Nagarjunakonda.
Both Sriparvata and Sriparvataswami refer exclusively to Nagarjunakonda.
accepted.x: Sriparvata refers to Nagarjunakonda or Vijayapuri, while Sriparvataswami was the family deity of the Vishnukundins and is identified with Srisaila Mallikarjuna.
accepted.tq: Separate look-alike names by their associated place and dynasty.
accepted.sec: Acharya Nagarjuna and Sriparvata - tradition, monastery, Sri Parvataswamy identified as Buddha (Kielhorn)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bodh Gaya and Sriparvata are respectively associated with which Buddhist traditions?
accepted.x: Bodh Gaya is associated with Hinayana, while Sriparvata is associated with Mahayana.
accepted.tq: Reversed-comparison trap between two Buddhist centres.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent tourism-related proposal connected with Nagarjunakonda?
o: The Archaeological Survey of India proposed a Nagarjunakonda–Bodh Gaya air corridor in May 2026.
A Palnadu Collector proposed an Amaravati–Nagarjunakonda rail service under the Integrated Buddhist Circuit in April 2025.
The Ministry of Culture proposed a Srisailam–Amaravati boat service under the Harappan Circuit in April 2026.
A Palnadu Collector proposed a Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam boat service and promoted Swadesh Darshan works in April 2026.
accepted.x: In April 2026, the Palnadu Collector visited the Nagarjunakonda Museum, proposed a Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam boat service and pushed Swadesh Darshan works.
accepted.tq: Current-affairs precision using date, office-holder role and scheme-name traps.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In May 2025, Miss World contestants visited Buddhavanam, which is being developed under the:
accepted.x: Buddhavanam, located next to Nagarjunakonda, is being developed under the Integrated Buddhist Circuit and was visited by Miss World contestants in May 2025.
accepted.tq: Scheme and event matching with a famous-word trap.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement correctly represents the FIRST/LAST distinction associated with Andhra’s religious history?
o: The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami, and the last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra was under the Ikshvakus.
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Sarvadeva, and the last royal Buddhist zenith was under the Vishnukundins.
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Pushpabhadraswami, and the last royal Buddhist zenith was under the Satavahanas.
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Hariti, and the last royal Buddhist zenith was under the Mauryas.
accepted.x: Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami is regarded as the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra, while the Ikshvakus represented the last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra.
accepted.tq: First-and-last comparison using paired historical distinctions.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
